messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — our hourly CSV export for 2026-02-15 has the 02:00–05:00 UTC slice all zeros for token_count. Invoice already posted and is ~12k tokens higher than the dashboard. attaching sample rows

alice_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the top ~10 rows of the export and your org_id so we can repro?

acme_ops: sure — org_id: org_62a7f8
```csv
org_id,hour,token_count
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T01:00:00Z,1432
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T02:00:00Z,0
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T03:00:00Z,0
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T04:00:00Z,0
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T05:00:00Z,0
org_62a7f8,2026-02-15T06:00:00Z,1788
```

ben_product: @carla_billing does the billing dashboard show those hours as zeros too or normal counts?

carla_billing: dashboard shows normal counts for 02–05 (non-zero). invoice shows the higher number. so raw export diverges. we need the raw export that generated the invoice and the post-processed CSV.

dmitri_eng: I’m looking at infra metrics. There was a restore of hourly_rollup_shard_7 around 2026-02-15T02:12Z (we pulled a snapshot after an incident). suspecting a race where the snapshot rehydrated files but the aggregator wrote zeros for that shard window. pulling logs now.

infra-bot: ```
[2026-02-15T02:10:57Z] restore: start snapshot=shard_7_snapshot_20260215
[2026-02-15T02:11:05Z] aggregator: flush hour=2026-02-15T02:00:00Z shard=7 rows=0
[2026-02-15T02:12:03Z] restore: complete snapshot=shard_7_snapshot_20260215
[2026-02-15T02:12:20Z] aggregator: rescan hour=2026-02-15T02:00:00Z shard=7 rows=0
```

dmitri_eng: that log timing aligns — looks like aggregator executed while restore was in-flight and produced zeroed rows. steps to confirm: run a quick query against the repstore and re-run extraction from raw events.

alice_support: Can you run these and paste results?
```sql
SELECT hour, sum(token_count) FROM hourly_rollups WHERE org_id='org_62a7f8' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-02-15T02:00:00Z' AND '2026-02-15T05:00:00Z' GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;
```
or if easier for ops:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://usage-exports/2026/02/15/hourly_shard_7.csv - | sed -n '1,20p'
```

acme_ops: I ran the S3 head and confirmed the CSV in the exports bucket has zeros (same as attached). I can grant support temporary access if needed.

acme_ops: granting support-team@redwood 24h access to the org export path.

ops_oncall: proposed remediation plan:
1) pause invoice processing for org_62a7f8
2) rehydrate shard snapshot and run the aggregator for hours 02–05 with dedupe so we don't double-count
3) regenerate CSVs and place at s3://usage-exports/reprocessed/2026/02/15/org_62a7f8/hourly.csv
4) notify customer and billing to adjust invoice if delta confirmed
ETA: ~3 hours if no infra blockers. :thumbsup:

carla_billing: please put invoice on hold for this org until we confirm the backfill. if delta > 100 tokens we'll adjust; if >10k we issue a credit.

ben_product: also want an alert for restore jobs where aggregator row_count == 0 for an affected time window — we shouldn't let silent zeros through.

dmitri_eng: running backfill now with a dry-run first. command I'm using:
```bash
python infra/tools/backfill_hourly.py --org org_62a7f8 --start 2026-02-15T02:00:00Z --end 2026-02-15T05:00:00Z --shard 7 --dry-run
```

dmitri_eng: dry-run shows missing tokens for three hours, expected delta +12432 tokens. proceeding with live run.

dmitri_eng: backfill complete — updated 3 hourly rows. regenerated CSV placed at:
`s3://usage-exports/reprocessed/2026/02/15/org_62a7f8/hourly.csv`
Delta: +12432 tokens for 02:00–05:00 UTC.

carla_billing: confirmed delta on reprocessed CSV matches dashboard. will apply credit and update invoice.

alice_support: acme_ops — sorry for the disruption. we resolved the export discrepancy and have a post-mortem scheduled. we'll share the timeline and action items (alert + dedupe hardening).

acme_ops: thanks all — appreciate the quick turn. :raised_hands:

dmitri_eng: action items: 1) add alert for aggregator zero-row after restore, 2) add a pre-commit check in restore workflow to quiesce aggregator, 3) add an automated backfill job for restore windows. filing follow-up tickets.

ops_oncall: locking thread until post-mortem posted.
